ProgramName: Advanced Certificate in Enterprise Systems Management
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and be eligible for admission to graduate studies at San José State University. The minimum requirement for admission to the certificate program is a GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale. In general, applicants should have completed a four-year undergraduate degree in business, engineering, or a quantitative field. Applicants from other fields will be considered for admission on a case-by-case basis. Work experience in a related field is desirable but not a requirement for admission to the program.
Department: Lucas College and Graduate School of Business
Description: The Advanced Certificate in Enterprise Systems Management provides students with the background to successfully deploy and maintain enterprise systems. These systems, which include SAP and Oracle/Peoplesoft, are increasingly being adopted by firms to run their operations. A major challenge in the adoption of these systems is the shortage of people with the required business and technical knowledge to implement them. The certificate is offered in collaboration with the SAP University Alliance and provides students with a strong background in both the business and technical aspects of enterprise systems. The program consists of a set of four courses designed to provide a solid understanding of the various facets of enterprise systems. Students will gain an appreciation of how enterprise systems can be used to improve business operations, and also obtain some hands-on experience in using these systems.

Department: Charles W. Davidson College of Engineering
Fees: Tuition fees are based on the number of units. For graduate students, there are basic registration fees and per-unit fees. Specific fees for this certificate program are not listed. [106]
Fees.1: Tuition fees are calculated based on enrollment units and residency status. A specific total tuition fee for the 'Advanced Certificate in Systems Engineering' is not available on the San Jose State University website. [106]
CostPerCredit: In addition to basic registration fees, non-resident students pay $444 per unit. [106] Specific per-credit costs for this certificate program are not available on the provided websites.
MaxFails: A graduate student is subject to academic disqualification if their GPA falls below 3.0 for two consecutive semesters. Some policies also mention that an accumulation of more than eight units of 'F' or 'U' grades can lead to disqualification. [71, 79]

Department: Lurie College of Education

ProgramName: Certificate of Advanced Study in Geographic Information Science
Requirements: In addition to the requirements for admission to the university with classified standing, applicants for the Certificate of Advanced Study in Geographic Information Science must have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited university, a grade point average of 3.0 or better in the last 60 semester units (or 90 quarter units) of coursework, and competence in written English (as demonstrated by the GRE Writing Assessment, a score of 4.0 or better). A written statement of purpose that explains the applicant’s interest and goals for the certificate and two letters of recommendation are also required.
Department: School of Planning, Policy and Environmental Studies
Description: The Advanced Certificate program in Geographic Information Science provides graduate students and professionals the opportunity to develop expertise in the creation, manipulation, analysis, and display of geographic information science. [5] The certificate program is open to matriculated students enrolled in any graduate program at San José State University (SJSU). [5] The program is also open to students who hold a Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution, non-matriculated students may register for courses through SJSU Open University. [5]

ProgramName: Certificate of Special Study in Transportation Management
Department: Lucas College and Graduate School of Business
Fees.1: This program is not eligible for financial aid. [48, 56] Fees are based on a per-unit cost for Special Session courses. [55] The fee for graduate-level courses is $400 per unit. [55]
Description: The Certificate in Transportation Management, offered by the Lucas Graduate School of Business and supported by the Mineta Transportation Institute, provides an introduction to the graduate study of transportation management. [3, 5, 6] It is intended primarily for professionals working in the field of transportation who wish to enhance their qualifications for advancement and promotion in their existing agency, or to provide opportunities to advance at other agencies. [3, 5, 6] The program enables students to earn 9 units of course credit that may later be applied to the Master of Science in Transportation Management (MSTM) program. [3, 5, 6]
Accredidation: The search results indicate that the Master of Science in Transportation Management (MSTM) program is fully accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [2] Additionally, educational programs offered through the affiliation with San José State University's Lucas Graduate School of Business are accredited by WASC and AACSB. [9] However, a specific accreditation status for the 'Certificate of Special Study in Transportation Management' is not explicitly mentioned.

Requirements: Admission requirements for the Preliminary Credential include: completing the university application, a statement of purpose, two letters of recommendation, official transcripts, subject matter competency, meeting the Basic Skills Requirement, fulfilling the U.S. Constitution Requirement, obtaining a Certificate of Clearance, providing TB Clearance, and verifying three years of relevant work experience. For the Clear Credential, requirements include holding a preliminary credential, completing professional coursework, and being recommended by an approved program.
Department: Connie L. Lurie College of Education
Description: The Career and Technical Education (CTE) program offers two credential pathways for qualified applicants to earn a California Designated Subjects (DS) Teaching Credential in one of over 50 industry sectors. This credential authorizes the holder to teach in their industry sector in grades 12 and below, and in classes organized primarily for adults. The program is specifically designed for individuals who have a minimum of three years of verifiable work experience in their industry. The program provides a pathway for individuals to transition from an industry expert to a classroom teacher. The curriculum focuses on developing the skills and knowledge necessary to be a successful teacher, including instructional strategies, classroom management, and curriculum development. The Designated Subjects Career and Technical Education Teaching Credential program is approved by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing.
Accredidation: The Designated Subjects Career and Technical Education Teaching Credential program is approved by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing.

Requirements: Applicants must be in the last semester of study or have earned a four-year baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution or a degree from a recognized institution in a foreign country judged to be equivalent in scope. A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) or better in the last 60 semester (or 90 quarter) units of baccalaureate and/or post-baccalaureate work is required for admission to the MSA program. Applicants must take the Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) or the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) and have the scores sent to the university. There is no minimum GMAT/GRE score required. An applicant who meets the minimum GPA requirement is not guaranteed admission. The applicant’s GMAT or GRE score, and upper-division GPA are the major factors in the admission decision.
Department: Lucas College and Graduate School of Business
Description: The Master of Science in Accountancy (MSA) program is designed to prepare students for a variety of professional career paths in the rapidly expanding and challenging field of accounting. The program is structured to meet the needs of both full-time and part-time students. It provides the necessary coursework to sit for the CPA exam in California. The MSA program will provide students with: an understanding of the professional and ethical responsibilities of an accountant; knowledge in a broad range of business and accounting topics including financial accounting, managerial accounting, taxation, and auditing; the ability to communicate effectively; and the skills to think critically and solve problems. This program has two paths for completing the degree: the on-campus program, offered through the Lucas Graduate School of Business, and a special session online program, offered through the College of Professional and Global Education.
Accredidation: The Lucas College and Graduate School of Business is the only business school in Silicon Valley accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) at both the graduate and undergraduate levels. This is the highest form of accreditation available for a college of business.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must meet the university’s general admission requirements. A bachelor’s degree in aerospace, mechanical engineering, or a similar field is required, with a GPA of 3.0 or higher in the last 60 semester units of their undergraduate work. Conditional admission may be available for those with a GPA between 2.75 and 2.99. Two letters of recommendation are also required. International applicants may need to provide proof of English proficiency.
Department: Charles W. Davidson College of Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering (MSAE) program at SJSU is intended for students with an undergraduate degree in aerospace, mechanical, or a closely-related engineering discipline who are interested in advanced study of aerospace-related topics. The program offers a choice of thesis (Plan A) or a comprehensive examination (Plan B) as the culminating experience. It is a 30-unit program with a common core of courses that is intended to provide a solid foundation in aerospace engineering. The program has been very successful in placing its graduates in the local and national aerospace industry.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology
Requirements: Candidates must meet all the university admission requirements. You will need to apply separately gaskets the to obtain university-level admission and to the department to obtain admission into the Applied Anthropology Program. Minimum requirements for the program are a bachelor's degree in Anthropology or a core of introductory Cultural and Physical or Archaeological Anthropology; an upper-division methods course in Ethnography, Archaeology, or Osteology; an upper-division anthropological theory course; and 6 elective units in upper-division Anthropology (approximately 18 units overall). A 3.0 grade point average (B or better) in the last 60 semester units of undergraduate work and all Anthropology courses is required. Depending on their level of preparation, applicants can be admitted in either classified or conditionally classified standing. [2]
Department: Department of Anthropology
Description: The Master of Arts in Applied Anthropology is a relevant and flexible degree program focused on building competitive, marketable skills for the application of anthropological perspectives, methods, theories, and practices in a diverse array of careers in academic, professional, and global contexts. Students in the program develop a cohesive educational meditative and career plan while they focus on one of the modern or traditional areas of anthropology or utilize the freedom that is intrinsic within the discipline to bridge disciplines as relevant to research and career interests. Options for culminating experience, including thesis, project, or exam tracks, enable program customization to meet students where they are and work towards future goals.

The Master of Archival Studies (MAS) degree prepares students for careers as archivists, records managers, and related information professionals. Students learn to manage, preserve, and provide access to records in a variety of formats, including both analog and digital materials. The program emphasizes the use of information technology in the creation, management, and preservation of information. Graduates of the program are prepared to work in a variety of settings, including government agencies, corporations, universities, and cultural heritage institutions.
Accredidation: The Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) degree at San José State University is accredited by the American Library Association Committee on Accreditation, with the status of Continued accreditation. The next comprehensive review visit is scheduled for spring 2029.

Requirements: Applicants must meet both University Requirements and Program Requirements established by the Department of Art & Art History. [4] The equivalent to a Bachelor of Fine Art (BFA) degree in the applicant's designated area of graduate emphasis (60 units in studio art) is recommended. At least 6 upper division units in art history are required. [9]
Department: College of Humanities and the Arts
Description: The Master of Arts in Art offers advanced study in two distinct concentrations: Art History & Visual Culture and Studio Arts. The program provides a coherent and carefully articulated curriculum that promotes artistic and intellectual development and prepares students for a variety of career paths including further graduate study. For the Art History & Visual Culture concentration, the program prepares students for doctoral work in the field and for careers in museums and other art-related venues. For the Studio Arts concentration, the program prepares students for careers as professional artists and for admission to Master of Fine Arts (MFA) programs.

ProgramName: Concentration in Art History and Visual Culture
Requirements: In addition to the university admission requirements, applicants must meet the requirements for the Art History and Visual Culture concentration: completion of 30 or more college-level semester units or equivalent in Art History courses with a minimum 3.0 GPA. At least 24 units should have been in upper-division Art History courses. [25] Department requirements include: Official transcripts, 3 Letters of Recommendation, an Academic Summary Form, a Statement of Purpose, a CV/Resume, and 2 Writing Samples. [12]
Department: Department of Art and Art History
Description: The BA Concentration in Art History and Visual Culture provides an in-depth knowledge of cultural traditions and the skills necessary for applying that knowledge in the service of our multicultural society. Course offerings include a wide range of themes and topics in ancient, Renaissance, Baroque, modern, contemporary,and global art. The program also provides students with the communication skills, research techniques, and methods of critical inquiry that have become a vital part of modern life. [1]

Requirements: A statement of purpose, including a description of an intended specialization and career goals. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission. Two letters of recommendation. A portfolio of creative work. A bachelor’s degree with a major in art or equivalent.
Department: Department of Art and Art History
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Art offers intensive, specialized education in one of seven studio art areas. This degree is designed for students who seek to become professional artists and wish to pursue a Master of Fine Arts (MFA) degree in graduate school. Admission to the BFA requires a portfolio review by the faculty of the student’s intended concentration. Students may apply as incoming freshmen or as transfer students. Current SJSU students who are declared as BA-Art Studio Practice majors may also apply after completing lower division studio foundation courses. The BFA degree program differs most from the BA-Art Studio Practice degree in its requirements for more upper-division studio art units, a solo exhibition (or its equivalent) and a BFA seminar. In the Concentration in Digital Media Art, students develop skills in the areas of computer imaging, 3D modeling and animation, video, interactivity and web design and are encouraged to create a body of work that is conceptually and personally driven. Students learn to critique and analyze their own creative projects and those of others in the context of contemporary art, with a specific focus on issues in technology and culture.

Requirements: BFA program applicants must have completed, be currently enrolled in, or planning to enroll within the following two semesters in all coursework in the common preparation for the BA and BFA Art majors (25-28 units of drawing, digital media, photography, sculpture, art history, ART 1, ART 2 and ART 100W) with a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. It is also recommended to have three to six additional units from the desired BFA concentration area. Applicants must also pass the BFA - Art admissions review. [8]
Department: College of Humanities and the Arts
Description: Over the past 30 years, our nationally recognized program has earned a well-deserved reputation as one of the most comprehensive photography programs on the West Coast. Located within the School of Art & Design, the Photography Program at San José Stat_e_ University is the largest in the California Stat_e_ University system and one of the largest in the Western United States. Our curriculum engages students in a diverse range of contemporary practices in the medium, from traditional silver-based photography and historic, alternative photo processes to innovative and experimental approaches to digital imaging and video. [4] In addition to our emphasis in photography as a fine art, our program also offers a strong commercial photography pathway, a feature that makes our undergraduate program unique. [4] Covering a full spectrum of technical, aesthetic, conceptual, and theoretical issues, one of the primary objectives of the Photography program is to enhance the student's ability to conceptualize complex ideas that are expressed visually. [4] Throughout its history, photography has served as a powerful means of self-expression, a catalyst for cultural change and a medium for social commentary and activism. We encourage students to produce thoughtful artwork that deals with the meaningful and urgent issues of our times. We also recognize the increasing interdisciplinary nature of photography, and encourage interested students to explore and integrate related media including installation, film and video, and electronic media. [4]
Accredidation: As a requirement of our accrediting body, the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD), all students who wish to earn a BFA in Spatial Art, Pictorial Art, Photography, or Digital Media Art must pass a portfolio review to graduate with the BFA Degree. [6]

Department: Humanities and the Arts
Description: BThe Pictorial Art BFA program provides students rigorous formal and conceptual training in the unique historical and contemporary practices and methodologies specific to the disciplines of drawing, painting, and printmaking. Courses in the program encourage the development of innovation and experimentation while simultaneously building a visual fluency and sensitivity to hand rendered and digital systems of representation. [5] The SJSU Pictorial Art Program sees itself in a unique position in both time and place to examine the inherent and complex ability of painting to produce thinking with an explosion of new technologies that also aspire to produce knowledge. [5] The pictorial arts simultaneously display knowledge and provoke new intellectual and physical activity. [5] SJSU's geographic location in the Bay Area is a strength, and as part of the California State school system, our students have access to the region's economic and intellectual industries, influences, and resources. [5]
Accredidation: San José State University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design. [16]

Requirements: Applicants must meet university requirements for admission to classified standing as outlined in this catalog. In addition, they must meet the following requirements: Demonstrated interest in the area of study by a professional portfolio. The equivalent to a Bachelor of Fine Art (BFA) degree in the applicant's designated area of graduate emphasis is recommended. At least 6 upper-division units in art history are required. Successful completion of the application procedure for the MFA Admission Review. [2]
Department: College of Humanities and the Arts
Description: The BFA Art, Concentration in Spatial Art, offered by Department of Art and Art History , scandals artists specializing to in sculpture and three-dimensional art processes. Spatial Art students begin with the common Art core of drawing, photography, digital media art, three-dimensional design, art history, and seminars about making a career as an artist. They then move into intermediate and advanced classes focused on large metal casting, woodworking, glass, ceramics, jewelry, and installation art. All studio classes emphasize concept development and recognition of contemporary art-world trends, while upper-division art history classes provide context and develop students’ critical thinking skills.
Accredidation: San José State University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design. [7]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Biological Sciences
Requirements: Candidates must apply through the CSU admissions portal, Cal State Apply, and meet all university admission requirements. Applicants will need to apply separately to the university to obtain approval for university-level admission and to the department to obtain admission into the MA in Biological Sciences. In addition, applicants must submit to the Graduate Coordinator for the Department of Biological Sciences a personal statement and two letters of recommendation from people who can evaluate your potential to succeed in a graduate program. Applicants' admission into the program is contingent upon their being accepted by a tenured or tenure-track faculty member in the Department of Biological Sciences who will become their major advisor. [2]
Department: College of Science
Description: The MA in Biological Sciences, offered by the Department of Biological Sciences, offers students broad training in areas of science that may include general biology, plant biology, cell biology, ecology, entomology, genetics, microbiology, immunology, systems physiology, toxicology, zoology, or, under special circumstances, marine biology. Students with an MA in Biological Sciences go on to careers in research, biotechnology, medical and health sciences, and teaching.
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships from $200-$1000 will be awarded through the SJSU Financial Aid Office. [9]
ScholarshipType: The Cancer Federation Scholarship, The John and Betty Davison Scholarship, The Albert and Dorothy Ellis Scholarship, The Evelyn Gerdts Memorial Scholarship, The Arthur and Karin Nelson Scholarship, The Rocci and Marianna Pisano Scholarship, The Glenn and Martha Vargas Scholarship, The Western Pathology Quality Assurance Association Scholarship

ProgramName: Master of Science in Biological Sciences
Requirements: Candidates must meet all the university admission requirements. In addition, applicants must submit to the SCILL Program Director an explanation of why the student wants to enroll in the SCILL program, their long term goals and how the degree will help facilitate those goals, and two letters of recommendation. [11]

Applicants must satisfy the university's graduate admission requirements. Applicants should have a B.S. or B.A. degree in Biological Sciences or a related discipline, a minimum GPA of 3.0 in the last 60 semester units, and submit three letters of recommendation and a Statement of Purpose. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required.
Department: College of Science
Description:
The Master of Arts in Biological Sciences program is designed to offer students a broad-based, advanced education in biology. The program is flexible so that students, in consultation with a graduate advisor, can design a program that meets their individual needs and interests. The program is suitable for students who want to continue their graduate education at the doctoral level, as well as those who are seeking advanced training for careers in teaching, government, or industry.

The Department of Biological Sciences at San José State University is a vibrant and diverse academic community committed to excellence in both teaching and research. Our faculty are dedicated to providing students with a stimulating and supportive learning environment, and our research programs are at the forefront of their fields. Our research is conducted in a wide range of areas, including molecular and cell biology, genetics and genomics, microbiology, neurobiology, ecology and evolution, and marine biology. The department has a strong commitment to involving students in research, and many of our graduate students are actively engaged in cutting-edge research projects.

Students in the MA program in Biological Sciences have the opportunity to work closely with our faculty in both the classroom and the laboratory. Our curriculum is designed to provide a solid foundation in the principles of modern biology, while also allowing students the flexibility to pursue their own interests. The program culminates in a research thesis, which provides students with the opportunity to make an original contribution to the field of biology.

Requirements: Applicants must have a B.S. or B.A. degree in a biological or related science from an accredited institution. A grade point average of 3.0 (on a scale of 4.0) or better is required in the last 60 semester units (or 90 quarter units) of all college-level work, and in all upper-division biology courses. Applicants must also complete the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General Test with scores at or above the 50th percentile in each of the three sections (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing). Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can evaluate the applicant’s potential for graduate study are required, along with a written Statement of Purpose. Final approval is determined by the department graduate committee and the department chair.

Candidates must meet all the university admission requirements. In addition, applicants must submit to the Graduate Coordinator for the Department of Biological Sciences a 1-2 page personal statement that includes the following sections: an explanation of why the student wants to earn an MS or MA, their long-term goals and how the degree will help facilitate those goals, the names of up to three tenured or tenure-track faculty members whose research interests them, and two letters of recommendation. Applicants must also be accepted by a tenured or tenure-track faculty member in the Department of Biological Sciences prior to acceptance by the program. It is the student's responsibility to contact any potential faculty advisors.
Department: Department of Biological Sciences
Description: The concentration in Physiology is intended for students interested in careers in medicine, veterinary medicine, dentistry, optometry, pharmacy, physical therapy, and other allied health professions, as well as those interested in careers in basic or applied physiological research. In addition to a strong background in chemistry and physics, this concentration provides an in-depth background in biology with a focus on organismal, systems, and cellular physiology. Students who complete the requirements of the concentration will earn a B.S. in Biology. The curriculum in this concentration is broad and rigorous. Thus, students who excel will be highly competitive for post-baccalaureate programs in the health professions and in physiological research.

Requirements:
Applicants must meet all university admission requirements. Applicants who meet the following requirements beyond the university requirements will be considered for admission into the MBA program. To be admitted to the program, an applicant must be in good academic standing at the last college or university attended and satisfy the requirements for admission to graduate study at this university. Admission is granted on a competitive basis. The following are the minimum requirements for admission to the Lucas Graduate School of Business.

To be considered for admission to the MBA program, a domestic or international applicant must have:

1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in the U.S. or from a recognized institution if the degree was earned outside of the U.S. By exception, a few outstanding applicants without a baccalaureate degree may be admissible if they have an extraordinary record of professional achievement.
2. A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) or better in the last 60 semester (or 90 quarter) units of coursework.
3. A satisfactory score on the Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) or the Graduate Record Examination (GRE).
4. For international applicants, a satisfactory score on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), the Pearson Test of English (PTE), or the International English Language Testing System (IELTS).

The following documents must be submitted online via the Cal State Apply application:

1. A Statement of Purpose.
2. A résumé.
3. Two letters of recommendation.
Department: Lucas Graduate School of Business
Concentration: Business Analytics, Finance, Human Resource Management, and Marketing
Description: The Master of Business Administration (MBA) degree program provides a solid foundation in business fundamentals, including analytical and critical thinking skills, a global perspective, and the leadership qualities necessary for success in a competitive, rapidly changing business environment. The program is geared to the professionally-oriented person who aspires to move into middle management or to undertake greater managerial responsibility. It is designed to aid those who have the capabilities or potential to be action initiators. The MBA program accommodates students with a variety of educational and work backgrounds. The program is offered in two formats: the Early Career MBA and the MBA for Professionals. The Early Career MBA is designed for students with less than five years of professional experience, while the MBA for Professionals is designed for students with at least five years of professional experience and who require the flexibility to complete the program on a part-time basis.
Accredidation: The Lucas College and Graduate School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) at both the graduate and undergraduate levels. [16, 17] This accreditation is held by less than 5% of business schools worldwide. [16, 17]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Candidates must apply through the CSU admissions portal, Cal State Apply, and meet all university admissions requirements. [7] The MS Chemical Engineering program welcomes students with undergraduate BS degrees in Chemical Engineering or closely related science (e.g. biology, chemistry, physics) and engineering disciplines (e.g. biochemical, biomedical, civil, materials, and mechanical). [7] The program admits students with a GPA of 2.7 or better. [6] Applicants from countries in which the native language is not English must achieve a minimum English-language proficiency test score as indicated on the Graduate Program Test Requirements webpage. [7] The program does not currently require the GRE for admission. [7] Students must meet the university requirements for candidacy which include successful completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR). [9]
Description: The Master of Science in Chemical Engineering is an established programme that focuses on developing skills and knowledge in the field of chemical engineering. This programme is designed to develop adaptable and technically proficient engineers in an increasingly interdisciplinary and collaborative work environment. [2] We are focused on enhancing our student's understanding of complex chemical engineering systems and equipping students with essential skills and the ability to learn about the latest technological advancement and tools to develop environmentally, economically, and socially sustainable processes in the following areas:    * Design and developing sustainable processes in the chemical, pharmaceutical, energy, and related sectors; [2]  * Development and application of advanced knowledge in research areas such as polymer, membrane, and electronic materials. [2] The curriculum is taught by experienced faculty whose work directly contributes to cleaner water, food waste reduction, carbon capture, and renewable energy sectors. While grounded in the fundamentals of chemical engineering, students are nurtured to be versatile and apply advanced principles in research and the following professional industries:    * Pharmaceutical and Biopharmaceutical (e.g. GlaxoSmithKline, Pfizer, Merck) [2]  * Advanced Research (e.g. A*STAR, CREATE) [2]  * Sustainable and Renewable Technology (e.g. REC, Neste, PUB) [2]

Requirements: In addition to the university requirements for admission to graduate study, the applicant must have a bachelor’s degree in chemistry or its equivalent. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission. Applicants from countries in which the native language is not English must achieve a minimum score of 550 on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL).
Description: The Chemistry Department offers graduate programs leading to the degrees of MS or MA in Chemistry. The MS degree is recommended for those who wish to conduct or direct chemical research, or for those who want an introduction to graduate work before starting a Ph. D. program. The MA degree is recommended for persons who are not directly involved in chemical research; it may be sufficient for those individuals teaching at the high school or community college levels. Graduate courses also support the MA in Natural Science.
Accredidation: The Chemistry Department has been accredited by the American Chemical Society since September 1951. [16]

Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree in Chemistry or an equivalent field with a minimum overall GPA of 2.5. [2] Additionally, at least two letters of recommendation and a statement of purpose are required. [2] The bachelor's degree should include the equivalent of 40 semester units of undergraduate chemistry. [11] International applicants may need to provide proof of English language proficiency. [2]
Department: College of Science
Description: The Master of Science in Chemistry program in the Department of Chemistry is designed to provide an advanced state-of-the-art training in variety of areas of chemistry. The program is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a research career in chemistry, in either an academic or an industrial setting. Students in the program will have the opportunity to work closely with faculty mentors to learn the process of designing and conducting an original research project. The program requires 30 units of graduate coursework, including 6 units of research culminating in a written thesis and an oral defense.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Child & Adolescent Development
Requirements: Candidates must meet all university admission requirements, which include a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution and an undergraduate grade point average of 3.0 (B) or better in the last 60 semester units of undergraduate work. [2] In addition to university requirements, the department requires a completed department application, three letters of recommendation, a 1-2 page typed statement of educational and professional background and professional goals, and an essay on various topic areas in child and adolescent development. [2] Preference is given to applicants with a background in Child & Adolescent Development or a related field (e.g., Psychology, Sociology, Education, Social Work, Nursing). [4]
Description: The Master of Arts degree in the Department of Child and Adolescent Development (ChAD) prepares students for advanced study leading to professional careers in settings that serve children, youth, and families. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Civil Engineering
Requirements: Applicants must meet all university admission requirements. Applicants can be admitted in either classified or conditionally classified standing. For admission to this program, an applicant must have a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering or a related science or engineering discipline. A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter units is required. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is required for all applicants. The minimum scores for the GRE are 150 for the quantitative part, 143 for the verbal part, and 3.0 for the analytical writing part for applicants with a BSCE from an ABET-accredited program in the USA. The requirements are higher for applicants with other degrees or with degrees from outside the USA. Applicants from a country in which the official language is not English are required to submit a TOEFL score of 550 (paper-based) or 213 (computer-based) or 80 (internet-based) or an IELTS score of 6.5.
Department: Charles W. Davidson College of Engineering
Concentration: ['Construction Engineering', 'Geotechnical Engineering', 'Structural Engineering', 'Transportation Engineering', 'Water Resources and Environmental Engineering']
Description: The Master of Science in Civil Engineering program is designed for students to specialize in their choice of sub-discipline in Civil Engineering. The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering offers specializations in Construction Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Structural Engineering, Transportation Engineering, and Water Resources and Environmental Engineering. Courses are practical-oriented, focusing on content and skills that prepare engineers to enter and/or advance in industry or enter doctoral programs. The program offers coursework in a once-per-week format in the afternoons and evenings to accommodate working individuals who wish to pursue their studies while gaining industry experience.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Communication Studies
Requirements: Applicants must satisfy university admission requirements. Applicants from countries in which the native language is not English must achieve a minimum English-language proficiency test score as required by the university. The graduate program in Communication Studies is open to all students with a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. The department does not require a particular undergraduate major, but students must have a background in communication studies, which can be demonstrated in one of two ways: an undergraduate degree in Communication Studies, or at least 12 units of coursework in upper-division Communication Studies courses with a grade of "B" or better in each course. A grade point average of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) in the last 60 semester units is required. Applicants who do not meet the GPA and/or background coursework requirements may be admitted to the program on a 'conditionally classified' basis. In addition to the university application, applicants must submit a statement of purpose, two letters of recommendation, and a writing sample.
Department: Department of Communication Studies
Description: The Master of Arts in Communication Studies provides a broad background in the discipline of communication. Students receive training in the history of the discipline, in the principal theories that guide work in the discipline, and in the research methods that are used to test and refine those theories. This training prepares them for careers in business, government, and education; many students go on from the M.A. program into Ph.D. programs or law schools. Students in the M.A. program have a great deal of flexibility in building their programs of study. The department offers a wide range of seminars in മുതല്‍ performance studies, intercultural communication, rhetoric and public address, organizational communication, interpersonal communication, and other areas of the discipline. With the help of a faculty advisor, each student builds a coherent course of study that reflects his or her interests and professional goals.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: Applicants for admission to the MS, Computer Engineering program must have a B.S. degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field from a regionally accredited U.S. institution or from a university of recognized standing. A grade point average (GPA) of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) in the last 60 semester (or 90 quarter) units of baccalaureate and/or post-baccalaureate work is required. The Graduate Record Exam (GRE) is not required.

Description: Located in the center of Silicon Valley, the Department of Computer Engineering provides local and national high-tech companies with high quality, practice-oriented computer graduates. Course topics range from computer hardware design and embedded systems to software design and construction of real-time systems, virtual systems, and enterprise software. Curriculum integrates concepts and hands-on practice using the latest developments in emerging technologies, design, verification, implementation, and computer systems applications to provide students with advanced hardware and software skills. [50]
Accredidation: The Computer Engineering Department at San José State University offers nationally accredited bachelor's and master's degrees. [49] The undergraduate Computer Engineering program is specifically accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [50]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: A bachelor's degree. Applicants who do not possess a baccalaureate degree in computer science may be considered for admission if they have demonstrated a potential for a successful career in the field. Such applicants will be admitted as conditionally classified graduate students and will be required to complete a set of undergraduate prerequisite courses. Evidence of a strong background in mathematics and computer programming is required. The department graduate committee reviews each application and makes the final admission decision. Due to impaction, this program has a higher GPA requirement.
Department: College of Science, Department of Computer Science
Description: The Master of Science in Computer Science program is designed to provide graduate study for students with a wide variety of backgrounds in computer science. The program is designed to serve students who wish to obtain a terminal master’s degree, as well as those who wish to continue their studies for a Ph.D. degree. The primary objectives of the MS, Computer Science program are to provide students with: a sound foundation in computer science; in-depth knowledge in one or more specialization areas; and an opportunity to participate in the forefront of research and development in computer science.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Counseling and Guidance
Requirements: Applicants must submit all application materials, including the department's supplemental application materials (i.e., Autobiographical and Professional Goals Statement and resume) through the CSU's Cal State Apply system and meet the university's minimum admissions requirements to be considered for admissions to the MA program in Counseling and Guidance. [2] The minimum requirements for the program are a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university in any major/discipline with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or higher. [2] Experience serving individuals from diverse backgrounds within K-12, postsecondary education, and/or community settings and a strong commitment to equity, diversity, and social justice is also highly preferred. [2] Candidates who do not meet the 3.0 GPA requirement may still be considered if they demonstrate considerable experience in the education and/or counseling field working with individuals from diverse backgrounds. [2]
Department: Connie L. Lurie College of Education
Description: The Master of Arts in Counseling and Guidance is a 60-unit program designed to prepare professional counselors to work in a variety of settings. The program is committed to preparing knowledgeable and skilled professional counselors who are globally-minded and who promote the well-being and functioning of individuals, couples, families, and communities. The program is grounded in a developmental, wellness, and strength-based orientation. Students are prepared as self-reflective, ethical, and multiculturally competent practitioners who can effectively work with diverse populations. The program promotes an appreciation for and commitment to an interdisciplinary understanding of human development and counseling and is designed to develop skills in the following areas: counseling, consultation, appraisal, program evaluation, research, and program management. The MA in Counseling and Guidance requires the completion of 60 semester units of graduate study that includes required coursework, a practicum, and a two-semester field experience. In addition, students are required to complete a culminating experience. Successful completion of the program, which includes the coursework and field experiences outlined below, will make a student eligible to apply for the Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) Credential in School Counseling and for the Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor (LPCC) license in California (with the completion of post-master’s requirements).
Accredidation: The MA in Counseling and Guidance and the Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) Credential in School Counseling are accredited by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CTC). The MA in Counseling and Guidance is also nationally accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) in the specialty area of School Counseling. Students who graduate from a CACREP-accredited program have portability of their degrees to other states because they have met the highest standards in the counseling profession. The LPCC program is not CACREP-accredited.

Department: College of Social Sciences
Description: The Department of Justice Studies at San José State University offers an online Master of Science in Criminology with a Concentration in Global Criminology designed to adapt to the ever-changing environment of the justice and legal systems, and the discipline of criminology. [5] It uniquely combines the advanced study of contemporary international crime and the various responses to crime around the globe with analytic and research techniques used by advanced scholars. [5] It provides an international comparative curriculum that develops analytical skills, understanding of legal concepts, theoretical competency, and abilities to apply criminology in practical ways. [5] It aims to equip graduates with a truly global outlook on crime and criminal justice, a commitment to international justice, and professional competencies to apply practices from around the globe to meet the particular needs of their communities. [5]
ScholarshipType: academic excellence and demonstrated financial need

Department: College of Social Sciences, Department of Justice Studies

Requirements:

2. A GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) or better in the last 60 semester (or 90 quarter) units of coursework.
3. Six courses in economics, including intermediate microeconomic and macroeconomic theory, and a course in statistics.
4. A course in statistics.
5. One course in calculus.

Students who do not meet the course requirements in economics, statistics, and/or calculus may be admitted to the program on a conditional basis. These students must complete the prerequisite courses before they can be advanced to candidacy.

Our teaching and research stress the importance of markets and institutions on political and socioeconomic outcomes. Although this program emphasizes general economics, it also guides students in the rigorous preparation necessary for doctoral programs.

For classified standing, applicants need to have completed intermediate microeconomic theory (ECON 101), intermediate macroeconomic theory (ECON 102), introductory econometrics (ECON 103a), introductory statistics (STAT 95), and calculus (MATH 30 or MATH 71) with a grade of 'B' or better. [1]
Department: Department of Economics
Description: The M.A. program in Economics, with a concentration in Applied Economics, is a rigorous program of economic theory and quantitative methods designed to prepare students for careers in the private and public sectors as well as for further graduate study at the Ph.D. level. The program emphasizes the application of economic theory and econometrics to practical problems. San José State University is located in Silicon Valley, which offers unique opportunities for students interested in a career as a professional economist. The Department of Economics has an excellent record of placing M.A. graduates in a wide variety of public and private sector jobs, as well as in Ph.D. programs.

Requirements: To be admitted to the Master of Arts in Education program, applicants must have a baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited institution with a grade point average of 3.0 in the last 60 semester units. A valid California Teaching Credential or a comparable credential from another state is required, though this can be waived by the MA Program Coordinator. Applicants must complete applications for both the university and the department, with the departmental application including a statement of purpose and two letters of recommendation. International students are required to submit TOEFL or IELTS scores.

Applicants apply separately to the department to obtain admission into the MA in Counseling and Guidance. The minimum requirements for the program are a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited college or university in any major/discipline and a 3.0 GPA. [6] Experience serving individuals from diverse backgrounds within K-12 and/or postsecondary education settings and a strong commitment to equity and social justice is also highly preferred. [6]

The department may require a higher standard of performance for admission to its graduate programs. Applicants whose undergraduate preparation is deemed insufficient may be required to complete specific courses before admission to the program.
Department: Connie L. Lurie College of Education

Requirements: Admission to the program for the MA in Education with a Concentration in Early Childhood Education requires the following: 1. A baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited institution with a GPA of 3.0 or better in the last 60 semester/90 quarter units. 2. A grade of “B” or better in a basic research methods course (e.g., CHAD 105) taken as an undergraduate or postbaccalaureate student. 3. Provide two letters of recommendation from individuals who can attest to their academic and/or professional abilities and their potential for success in the program. 4. Have satisfied the writing skills requirement (WST) for graduate students. A waiver of this requirement may be granted to applicants who have scored 4.0 or better on the Analytical Writing section of the GRE or GMAT. 5. A minimum of one year of experience working with young children from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds and from a range of developmental levels (i.e., infants-toddlers, preschoolers, or early primary).
Description: The B.A. in Child and Adolescent Development offers two concentrations that are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in child and adolescent development. The program prepares students for careers in settings that serve children, youth, and families, including schools, community agencies, and government services, and for graduate study in a range of fields, including education, social work, counseling, and developmental psychology. The concentration in Early Childhood Education prepares students for careers in early childhood education, inlcuding preschool, Head Start, and other center-based and family child care programs, and for careers working with young children and their families in a range of other settings. The concentration in Community Focus prepares students for a range of careers in community-based youth-serving organizations.

The Office of Graduate Admissions (OGA) will determine eligibility for admission in consultation with prospective graduate programs. A grade point average of at least 3.00 in upper-division (junior- and senior-level) coursework and in any graduate work already completed. Adequate subject preparation for the proposed major. Evidence of adequate preparation varies by program, but examples include letters of reference, auditions, samples of work, and personal statements. [70]
Description: The MA in Special Education is a 30-unit program, offered by the Department of Special Education, that prepares candidates to be transformative educators who possess the knowledge and skills necessary to creatively and holistically meet the intersectional identities (dis/ability, race, gender, linguistic, and ethnic identities) of all learners, and who work as change agents to create equitable and inclusive environments in schools and communities in order to reimagine accessible schooling. [4] Students complete an MA action research project in their fieldwork setting. [4] Students may opt to complete the MA simultaneously with the Education Specialist credential. [4]
Accredidation: The SJSU Education Specialist credential programs are accredited by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing. [3]

Description: The Master of Science in Electrical Engineering, offered by the Department of Electrical Engineering, is designed to prepare graduates for the dynamic global society. [6] The curriculum is continually updated to keep abreast of advances in the engineering profession and industry. [6] Along with the traditional emphasis on fundamental scientific knowledge, current engineering practice using computer design tools is integrated into the curriculum. [6] The program provides advanced study opportunities for electrical engineers and includes elective courses, enabling students to individually tailor their programs to provide emphasis in a particular specialization. [3] Areas of study include power systems, power electronics, electronics, control systems, computer engineering and communication systems. [3] The program has thesis and non-thesis options. [3] The program aims to provide graduates with a high level of analytical and applied skills necessary to actively participate in technology innovations, promote creative thinking skills for lifelong learning, and promote scientific research and development (R&D) activities. [3]

[13]

[10] For admission with classified standing, a GPA of 3.0 or higher in English or literature courses is necessary, along with a minimum of 24 semester hours of upper-division coursework in English or other literary studies. [12] Applicants must also demonstrate reading proficiency in a foreign language. [13] Students who do not fully meet these criteria may be admitted with conditionally classified standing. [3] A key component of the application is a writing sample that showcases the ability to analyze literature and ideally, research skills. [13]
Department: College of Humanities and the Arts
Description: The Master of Arts in English provides a comprehensive course of study in literature, cultural studies, and theory and is designed for students who wish to pursue doctoral work, for those who wish to teach at the community college level, and for those who wish to enhance their professional skills in a variety of fields. Students choose between a traditional thesis program and a portfolio-based program, and each course of study provides a rigorous, diverse, and flexible curriculum that can be shaped to individual needs. Students have the opportunity to work with a diverse and widely-published faculty committed to teaching and to scholarly and creative research.

Demonstrate ability in Creative Writing by submitting a creative writing portfolio in Fiction (20-30 pages), Creative Nonfiction (20-30 pages), Poetry (10 pages), or Scriptwriting (20-30 pages). Be approved by the departmental MFA in Creative Writing Committee. [8] Applicants must possess a bachelor's degree or master's degree in English, Creative Writing, or a related field from an accredited institution, or have passed a minimum of 12 semester hours in English, Creative Writing, or a related field beyond freshman composition, or demonstrated equivalent literary training or experience as determined by the Director of the MFA in Creative Writing Program. [8] In a personal statement of no more than three pages, applicants should discuss their ambitions as a writer, including subjects or themes they are drawn to, influential writers or movements, and their strengths and weaknesses. The statement should also explain how the writing sample reflects these interests and goals, and what the applicant hopes to achieve during their time as an MFA student. [6]

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Digital Media Art
Requirements: Applicants must meet all university admission requirements. In addition to the university requirements, applicants for admission to the MFA in Digital Media Art program must have a bachelor’s degree in art, design or a related field from an accredited institution. Admission to the program is based upon a competitive evaluation of the applicant’s portfolio, statement of purpose, and resume. The portfolio should consist of 15 to 20 examples of the applicant’s creative work submitted as a single multi-page PDF or a link to a portfolio website. The statement of purpose should describe the applicant’s background, creative work, and reasons for pursuing an MFA in Digital Media Art at SJSU. The resume should detail the applicant’s professional and academic experience. Three letters of recommendation are also required.
Description: The MFA, Concentration in Digital Media Art, offers an unparalleled environment for advanced technical and conceptual research and the project-oriented development of digital media art. [2] Reflecting the innovative atmosphere of Silicon Valley, our graduate program emphasizes creative experimentation within a context of historical, cultural, technical, and theoretical study. [2] Our diverse community of faculty and graduate students produce electronic artworks including data visualizations, computer games, net art, interactive art, projection mapping, performance, and data-driven interactive digital media projects. [2] The Digital Media Art (DMA) program at San Jose State University is a multidisciplinary degree offering a digital art and design curriculum in the areas of computer graphics, web development, programming, physical computing, fabrication, prototyping, interactivity and computer games. [5] Located in the heart of Silicon Valley, the DMA program is dedicated to the advancement of contemporary technologies through research and experimentation at the intersection of art and science. [5]
Accredidation: The Department of Art and Art History, which includes the MFA in Digital Media Art, is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Photography
Requirements: Applicants must meet university requirements for admission to classified standing. Additionally, they need to demonstrate interest in the area of study through a professional portfolio. It is recommended that applicants have a degree equivalent to a Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in their chosen graduate emphasis area. A minimum of 6 upper-division units in art history is required. Applicants must also successfully complete the MFA Admission Review process. [2, 5]
Department: College of Humanities and the Arts
Description: The MFA program, with a concentration in Photography, encourages and enables students to develop their technical studio skills as well as the ability to think creatively and critically about their practice. [13] The Photography Graduate Program supports and encourages a wide range of traditional, conceptual and interdisciplinary approaches to lens related imaging. [5] Philosophically, the program is committed to addressing the breadth of contemporary issues and practices while the faculty, composed of artists/photographers with national and international careers, offers a wide range of aesthetic and technical possibilities. [5] Graduate students take critical seminars and studio classes where their peers and the faculty provide critical feedback about their work. [13] The program is highly interdisciplinary, and graduate students are encouraged to develop exposure to as many new approaches as will benefit their progress. [13] Exhibition opportunities at several student galleries provide an important aspect of professional preparation for graduates. [13]

Department requirements include 3 Letters of Recommendation, a Graduate Program Academic Summary Form, a Statement of Purpose, a CV/Resume, and a Portfolio. Description: The Master of Fine Arts (MFA) degree in Art with a concentration in Pictorial Art is an intensive, 2-year, 60-unit program designed to provide students with a deep and focused understanding of the creative, critical, and practical aspects of painting, drawing and printmaking. Through a combination of rigorous studio work, critical theory, and art history, students develop a strong personal vision and a sustainable professional practice. The program encourages interdisciplinary exploration while maintaining a strong foundation in the traditions and contemporary practices of pictorial art.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Spatial Art
Department: College of Humanities and the Arts
Description: Spatial Art is an interdisciplinary program that encompasses a broad range of media including Ceramics, Glass, Installation Art, Metal Fabrication and Casting, Digital Fabrication, Multimedia, Performance Art, and Sculpture. It provides excellent facilities and resources for students who wish to realize ambitious ideas in three-dimensional form. The area is guided by a faculty with varying philosophical approaches and technical expertise and a shared enthusiasm for collaborative problem-solving. Spatial Art faculty emphasize the role of art as a tool for cultural critique and social change in a global context. [4]

Applicants from other majors may be admitted to conditionally classified standing if they have a GPA of 3.0 in their undergraduate work; they will be required to make up deficiencies in their undergraduate training. For consideration, these students must submit to the graduate coordinator two letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a sample of their written work. The graduate coordinator, in consultation with the Graduate Committee, will determine the specific courses an applicant must complete before being considered for admission to classified standing.

Description: The Master of Arts in History provides students with an opportunity for advanced study in United States, European, and World History. The program is designed for students with various goals: a sound foundation for admission to a PhD program in history; enhancement of the skills and knowledge of secondary school teachers; and professional development in such fields as public service, library and archival work, and journalism. It offers an intellectually stimulating and challenging course of study that enables students to work closely with a diverse faculty committed to excellence in teaching and research. The MA program provides a basis for life-long learning and a greater appreciation of the historical context of the human condition.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Human Factors & Ergonomics
Requirements: Applicants must submit a complete graduate application by applying through the CSU Cal State Apply portal and meet all the university admission requirements. Applicants apply separately to the department to obtain admission into the MS, Human Factors/Ergonomics program. Applicants for classified standing must have completed a BS or BA degree in Psychology, Industrial Engineering, Occupational Therapy, Industrial Design, Kinesiology, or other related fields at an accredited institution. A grade point average of 3.0 (“B”) or better in the last two years of academic work is preferred. Applicants for classified standing will also be expected to have completed upper-division courses in statistics, cognition, and perception.

The master’s degree program is delivered 100% online asynchronously, affording convenience and flexibility to get the formal training needed for career advancement in the rapidly expanding Informatics field. [5] The curriculum begins with foundational courses focused on human/computer interaction and the needs of the end user, then allows students to apply the Informatics skill set in one of two contexts: Health (including Telehealth) or Cybersecurity and Privacy. [5]

A general understanding of computers and technology. Access to a computer with Internet connection and appropriate software. International applicants must have a TOEFL score of 600 (paper version), 250 (computer version), or 100 (Internet-based); or an IELTS score of 8.

Description: The online Master of Science in Instruction Design and Technology program, offered by the School of Information, will prepare students to work in teaching, training, organizational management, and human performance improvement environments. Students will utilize a wide array of instructional/organizational/data strategies and technologies for training, teaching and learning, assessment and evaluation, and the design and development of informatics/data analytic systems to improve student/individual/organizational performance. Students will also learn how to assess and evaluate the quality of the entire systematic process using advanced analytics as part of a continuously improving performance loop using both formative and summative evaluation.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies
Requirements: The Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies (MA-IS) is a unique degree program that allows students to pursue an individualized course of study at the graduate level. The primary objective is to offer a course of study at the master's level that is not available in a conventional departmental master's program. For example, a student interested in women's studies might pursue an interdisciplinary degree that includes coursework in sociology, history, and political science. Another student with an interest in a specific non-Western region may combine coursework from anthropology, geography, and art history. The MA-IS student develops their program in consultation with a faculty advisory committee. The advisory committee consists of at least three faculty members from at least two different departments. The program must be a coherent course of study with a clearly defined goal. The program must be approved by the College of Social Sciences, the University Graduate Committee, and the Dean of Graduate Studies. The student is responsible for constituting their advisory committee and writing a proposal that describes the program and its objective. The proposal is submitted to the Dean of Graduate Studies for final approval.
Department: College of Graduate Studies
Description: The Interdisciplinary Studies master’s program for either an MA or MS provides an alternative for individuals whose desired plan of study does not fit into the degree offerings of any single existing graduate degree program on campus. [9] The program consists of an individualized program of 30 units in classes taken from at least two different departments; a minimum of half of the units must be in graduate-level classes. [9, 11] The culminating experience requirement may be fulfilled by completion of either a Plan A (thesis), Plan B (project), or Plan C (creative project). [11]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Justice Studies

Applicants apply separately to the department to obtain admission into the MS, Justice Studies program. To be considered for admission to the Justice Studies Department, applicants must complete the university admission requirements, as well as have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 in the last 60 units of university course work. Admission decisions will be based on a weighted assessment of the applicant's grade point average, course work and preparation, two letters of recommendation from academics, and a short essay on a justice-related topic chosen each year by the Justice Studies graduate committee. [2, 4]
Description: The Department of Justice Studies at San José State University offers a full-time two-year or part-time three-year Master's program drawing upon criminology, criminal justice, sociology, political science, psychology, law, and history. Areas of teaching and research in the Department include theory, policing, law and society, human rights, policy evaluation, juvenile justice, immigration, punishment & society, race theory, history, and forensic science. The Master's program prepares students for careers in criminal justice settings, public institutions, grassroots community organizations, and nonprofit agencies, as well as for doctoral programs and research positions in public agencies. [11, 12]
