Applicants must also satisfy the Graduate English requirement.
Department: College of Health and Human Sciences
Concentration: ['Exercise Physiology', 'Movement Science', 'Sport Management', 'Psychosocial Aspects of Sport and Physical Activity', 'Individualized Specialization']
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Kinesiology program allows students to pursue various interests and goals, including but not limited to promoting wellness, influencing the sport and fitness industry, and addressing psychological and sociological dynamics underlying performance and physical activity. [1] Within this diverse discipline, students may choose one of five different specializations to guide their program of study: Exercise Physiology, Movement Science, Sport Management, Psychosocial Aspects of Sport and Physical Activity, and Individualized Specialization - Designed for students with goals not represented above. [1] The Master of Science (M.S.) in Kinesiology is a 30 unit program. [1] To complete the program, students must take two core research methods classes, two to four specialization subcore classes, two to five elective classes, and a culminating project. [1]

The Master of Science degree in Kinesiology with a Concentration in Athletic Training is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE). The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the prevention, examination, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation of emergent, acute or chronic injuries and medical conditions. The program prepares students to sit for the Board of Certification (BOC) examination.
Accredidation: The Master of Science degree in Kinesiology with a Concentration in Athletic Training is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Athletic Training Education (CAATE).

ProgramName: Master of Library and Information Science
Requirements:
Applicants who meet the following requirements will be considered for admission in the Master of Library and Information Science program:

A bachelor's degree from any regionally accredited institution in any discipline with an overall GPA of at least 3.0 in the bachelor's degree or in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter units. [4]
A general understanding of computers and technology. [4]
Access to a computer with Internet connection and appropriate software. [4]
International applicants must have a TOEFL score of 600 (paper version), 250 (computer version), or 100 (Internet-based); or an IELTS score of 8. [4]

Note: We do not require a GMAT or GRE test, letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, or a resume. [4] Therefore, please do not include any of these in your application. [4]
Department: School of Information
Description:
The Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) degree program prepares graduate students for careers as information professionals. Graduates work in a variety of information environments, including libraries, archives, and any organization where information and knowledge are created, managed, and preserved. Our MLIS graduates are prepared for a future of new and evolving information formats, changing user needs, and emerging technologies.

The mission of the School of Information is to empower our diverse student population to be successful as information professionals in a global, digital environment.

Students in the MLIS program learn to be reflective practitioners who are skilled in providing equitable and inclusive access to information and who can think critically to solve problems that confront all types of information organizations.
Accredidation: The Master of Library and Information Science program is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA) Committee on Accreditation.
MaxFails: A graduate student is placed on academic probation if their cumulative GPA falls below 3.0. Failure to raise the cumulative GPA to 3.0 in the following semester results in disqualification.
ScholarshipType: Special Session Scholarships, Endowed and Donated Scholarships, Diversity Scholarships

Description: Linguistics, the scientific study of human language, explores what language is, how it works, and which properties human languages have in common. Our curriculum focuses on understanding how different aspects of language work and on how the languages of the world work and on how this understanding can be applied to support our culturally diverse society. Students in the Department of Linguistics and Language Development (LLD) are part of an ethnically and linguistically diverse student body, taught by nationally and internationally recognized faculty. Our research infrastructure includes a state-of-the-art computer lab, a phonology lab, and access to computerized language data. Approximately 25% of our students come from other countries and contribute greatly to our programs. The MA Linguisticssighted program students an provides with interdisciplinary education in the scientific study of language. Courses in general linguistics develop the ability to analyze data, to propose and refine theories about how language works. Elective courses in computational linguistics serve students interested in speech technology and natural language processing. Other electives in sociolinguistics, multilingualism, and applied linguistics emphasize the role of language in society, including in education, and language variation and change. Graduates in linguistics offer a set of highly specialized skills to IT companies and to organizations whose work places a premium on communication with linguistically diverse audiences. Many graduates pursue careers with companies specializing in these areas. Other graduates pursue teaching careers in language and linguistics in domestic and overseas institutions. A smaller but significant number of linguistics graduates enter PhD programs for more advanced study.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Materials Engineering
Requirements: A GPA of 2.7 or better with a B.S. in Materials Engineering or a closely related science (Biology, Chemistry, Physics) or engineering (Chemical, Electrical, Mechanical, Biomedical) degree is required. [27, 28] For international students, an acceptable English Language Proficiency exam score is necessary. [27, 28] The GRE is not required. [27, 28]
Department: Charles W. Davidson College of Engineering
Description:
The MS Materials Engineering program provides advanced study of materials engineering topics with an emphasis on both the fundamental and applied aspects. A multidisciplinary approach to education is evident in the materials engineering program’s specialization areas of semiconductor processing, polymers, ceramics, structural materials, and biomaterials. Elective courses are also available in science, business, and other engineering fields. This broad-based, multi-disciplinary educational program has proven to be an important factor for a student’s future success including leading Silicon Valley companies and in Ph.D. programs. 

Class schedules are designed for the convenience of employed engineers who wish to pursue graduate work on a part-time basis. Faculty are actively involved in research areas including electronic and magnetic materials, nanomaterials, energy materials, structural materials, computations, polymers, composites, and biomaterials. Research activity is sponsored by local industries as well as by government funding agencies. The MS Materials Engineering program welcomes students with undergraduate degrees in Materials Engineering or related science (biology, chemistry, physics) or engineering (chemical, electrical, biomedical, mechanical) degrees.

Department: College of Science
Description: This degree, offered by SJSU’s Department of Mathematics and Statistics is recommended for future community college teachers and for students who plan to continue toward the PhD in mathematics.
ScholarshipType: SJSU campus scholarships, Department scholarships, Private scholarships, Merit-based, Need-based

Description: The Master of Science in Mathematics is recommended for students who are preparing for a career in industry or government, or who intend to continue their studies toward a Ph.D. in mathematics. It provides the student with a solid foundation in mathematics that can be used as a stepping stone to a more specialized career. A student must pass 30 units of course work. In addition, a student must either pass two comprehensive exams or write a thesis or a project while under the supervision of a math department faculty member. Students will develop their mathematical understanding and problem-solving skills through a variety of theoretical and applied courses taught by our expert faculty. The M.S. degree is a flexible degree with students having many choices for their course of study. A student who wishes to specialize in a particular area of mathematics can do so by carefully selecting a set of courses and a thesis/project topic in that area.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Description: The Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering program provides students with an education tailored for professional practice in mechanical engineering. Students in the program benefit from: World-Class Faculty: a flexible curriculum that accommodates the needs of both full-time students and working professionals, the Mechanical Engineering program prepares its graduates to serve as technical specialists and leaders in corporate, industrial, and governmental careers.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Medical Product Development Management
Description: Students in the Master of Science in Medical Product Development Management degree program develop proficiency in applying leadership, management and decisionmaking skills in a regulated environment; understanding and conversing with others in a multi-disciplinary field; and understanding ethical, business, financial, global, and strategic implications in medical product development. [1] The MPDM program prepares students to enrich their communities as ethical and socially responsible graduates in a field in which the highest levels of integrity are a fundamental necessity. [1]

The Master of Science in Meteorology prepares students for high-level professional responsibility, independent research, and continued graduate work in atmospheric science. [2, 8] Graduate-level theoretical and applied meteorology courses and a substantial research project lead to the preparation of the master’s thesis, the culmination of the degree plan of study. [2, 8] Departmental opportunities for financial support include research and teaching assistantships. [2, 8] The Department of Meteorology and Climate Science has one of the most active research programs at SJSU. [2, 8]

The Master of Music graduate program in the School of Music and Dance offers training for careers in performance, conducting, composition, music education, research, and teaching. We also provide preparation for further advanced study in six distinct areas: Choral Conducting, Composition, Instrumental Conducting, Jazz Studies, Music Education, and Performance. Our MM, Music degree program is a 30-unit course of study, typically taken in four semesters over two years, and consists of graduate seminars, one-on-one private lessons, performance ensembles, and area of specialization coursework. The program culminates with the master’s exam and the completion of a graduate recital, project, or thesis.
Accredidation: The School of Music and Dance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Description: The Valley Foundation School of Nursing master’s degree program prepares leaders in advanced practice roles as nurse educators and family nurse practitioners. The program provides a foundation for doctoral study. The mission of the School of Nursing is to prepare a diverse community of students to become professional nurses who promote health and well-being, to provide leadership, and to be responsive to the health care needs of multicultural communities. The school is dedicated to providing an inclusive learning environment that prepares nurse leaders for evidence-based professional practice and engages in scholarly activities to advance the science and practice of nursing. The MS, Nursing degree program has two areas of concentration: Nurse Educator and Family Nurse Practitioner. Graduates of the Family Nurse Practitioner concentration are eligible to take certification examinations from the American Nurses Credentialing Center or the American Academy of Nurse Practitioners. Graduates of the Nurse Educator concentration will have the required coursework to take the Certified Nurse Educator examination. All students are admitted to a specific concentration. Students in the Family Nurse Practitioner and Nurse Educator concentrations are admitted as a cohort and progress through the program in a specified sequence of courses.
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master’s degree program in nursing, and post-graduate APRN certificate program at San Jose State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org).

Description: A graduate of this program is prepared for advanced nursing practice with a focus as a Nurse Educator (NE). [3] The program prepares nurses to assume the highest levels of professional nursing practice via courses which cover advanced theoretical knowledge, leadership development, assessment skills, and advanced teaching-learning practice. [2] Students will have an opportunity to critically evaluate and apply nursing theory and research as a scientific base for nursing practice. [2]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Nutritional Science
Description: The Master of Science in Nutritional Science program is designed to meet the needs of the student who has a baccalaureate degree and seeks advanced preparation in nutrition science, nutrition education, geriatric nutrition, and foodservice/restaurant management and packaging. [2] The program is intended to prepare candidates to assume leadership roles in their profession and communities and to provide the opportunity to acquire a foundation for doctoral study. [2]
Accredidation: In the process of fulfilling requirements for the MS degree, it is possible to complete the academic requirements of The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics toward becoming a registered dietitian. [7]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Occupational Therapy

Description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers the Master of Science (MS) in Physics. The MS degree may be earned with a thesis (Plan A) or without a thesis (Plan B). The MS in Physics is a 30-unit program. It is an excellent preparation for students who may wish to pursue a PhD in physics or a related field, as well as those who are seeking physics-related careers in teaching or industry with a master’s degree. Students are mentored by faculty who are actively engaged in research. Graduate students have opportunities to participate in forefront research in AMO (atomic, molecular, and optical) physics, computational physics, condensed matter physics, and physics education.

The Master of Public Administration (MPA) program at San José State University is the only accredited MPA program in the Silicon Valley. It is one of the most respected programs in the nation and has been for over 50 years. The MPA is a professional terminal degree for those who wish to work in public service. The MPA program prepares graduate students for administrative leadership, policy, and analyst positions in government, nonprofit agencies, and private corporations that work with government agencies. The program teaches the broad-based skills of a generalist and the specific skills of a specialist. Students are taught and mentored by a large, professionally-diverse faculty who are committed to preparing students to be leaders and managers who can bring positive change to their communities. The program is flexible to meet the professional goals and interests of a wide range of students.
Accredidation: The Master of Public Administration (MPA) program at San José State University is the only accredited MPA program in the Silicon Valley. It is one of the most respected programs in the nation and has been for over 50 years.

Description: The Master of Public Health (MPH) program is the professional degree for those who wish to work in the field of public health. The mission of the San José State University Master of Public Health Program is to provide the highest quality academic preparation for future public health leaders. We work with our community partners to create a healthier, more equitable future for all by taking a social justice-oriented, participatory, and community-driven approach to public health. Students in our program develop the skills to assess community needs, and to plan, implement and evaluate public health programs and policies in a variety of settings. The program improves the health and well-being of the populations of the San José community, the State of California, the nation and the world, by providing an accessible, high-quality education to a diverse student population. We are committed to graduating skilled public health professionals and leaders, as well as to creating, communicating, and applying knowledge to address the public health issues of the 21st century. The MPH degree program is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Accredidation: The MPH degree program is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

Description: The Master of Public Policy (MPP) is the professional degree for students seeking a career in policy analysis and public service. The program provides students with a strong foundation in public policy, management, and analysis. Students learn to develop, implement, and evaluate public policies in a variety of settings. The curriculum has a strong applied public policy and social science research emphasis, providing graduates with the research skills necessary for policy analysis and evaluation and the management skills to be successful in a public service career. The MPP program provides students with the unique opportunity to study public policy in the heart of Silicon Valley and the San Francisco Bay Area, an area with a number of innovative policy and service delivery approaches.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Quality Assurance
Description: The Master of Science in Quality Assurance (MSQA) is an interdisciplinary program that has been developed in partnership with quality assurance professionals from a variety of local industries including biomedical, software, high-tech, and service. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary for designing, implementing, and managing quality systems. Students will learn the principles of quality assurance and be prepared for careers as quality professionals with the ability to contribute to the improvement of organizational performance. The curriculum provides the necessary breadth and depth to ensure students have the skills to implement quality systems in a variety of industries. The program is designed for working professionals and all courses are offered in the evening. This is a self-support program offered through the College of Professional and Global Education (CPGE).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Software Engineering
Concentration: ['Enterprise Software Technologies', 'Cloud Computing and Virtualization', 'Data Science', 'Software Systems Engineering']
Description: The Master of Science in Software Engineering is a 30-unit program that is designed to develop the technical and managerial skills of software engineers. It provides the foundation for those who will be responsible for software quality and the process of software development, from initial specification to the final validation and verification. The curriculum provides an appropriate balance of theory and practice for the design, implementation, and evaluation of software. The program has four specializations: Enterprise Software Technologies, Cloud Computing and Virtualization, Data Science, and Software Systems Engineering.

The Master of Arts in Sociology prepares students for advanced study in sociology as well as for careers in community college teaching, government, and private industry. The graduate program provides a solid foundation in sociological theory, research methods, and a variety of substantive areas of study. The Sociology Department is committed to giving students 'hands-on' experience in all phases of the sociological enterprise. Toward that end, our graduate seminars emphasize close student-faculty interaction and many provide the opportunity for students to pursue their own research interests. In addition to regular course work, students can work with faculty on research projects and participate in professional conferences and workshops. Upon completion of the program, our students have the knowledge and experience necessary to pursue careers in research, teaching, or administration.

The Master of Science in Statistics is designed to prepare students to become practicing statisticians. It features theoretical and applied coursework in statistics, advanced statistical techniques, and skills-based coursework that emphasizes communication skills and provides practical experience. The program was developed in concert with industry and is designed to dovetail into professional career opportunities. Persons with bachelor’s degrees in engineering, the sciences, economics, business, the social sciences or other fields that use statistics are encouraged to apply. Those with bachelor’s degrees in mathematics or statistics are also welcome to apply for the program in order to advance their technical and theoretical skills.

The Master of Arts Teaching (MAT) degree program, offered by the Department of Teacher Education , prepares students to engage in social justice teaching practices, contribute to the development of cultural literacy, provide education that promotes democracy, and develop content knowledge expertise to teach in urban and suburban schools. [9] All the program courses will prepare enrolled students to provide instruction for multilingual learners and students with disabilities in general education classrooms. [9] Enrolled students also will learn to set up a supportive classroom environment based on social-emotional learning principles and experience collaborative co-teaching experiences with successful mentor teachers in the field. [9] Finally, students will design, carry out, and report on classroom-based teacher inquiry. [9] The MAT is earned in combination with a teaching credential and is not a stand-alone Master's Degree. [9]

The RTVF concentration provides professionally-oriented, hands-on training for students who seek careers in media production, post-production, and media management. Students are prepared to become multi-skilled media professionals, learning how to write, produce, direct, and edit for single- and multi-camera, studio, and field productions. Productions include a wide range of genres, from narrative and documentary films to entertainment and sports television, to commercials and corporate videos. Students also learn media management principles, including how to develop and pitch new programming, and how to distribute, market, and program media content.

The Lucas College and Graduate School of Business is the accrediting body for this program. The college is accredited by the AACSB International at both the graduate and undergraduate levels, a distinction that is held by less than 5% of business schools worldwide. The Master of Science in Taxation (MST) program is designed for students with an undergraduate degree in accounting who wish to specialize in taxation. The program provides students with a thorough knowledge of the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury Regulations, as well as an understanding of the process by which these laws and regulations have evolved and continue to change. Students learn to research tax issues, to communicate their findings, and to develop tax-planning strategies. They also become thoroughly familiar with the rules of professional conduct applicable to the tax practitioner.
Accredidation: The Lucas College and Graduate School of Business is accredited by the AACSB International at both the graduate and undergraduate levels.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL)
Description: The M.A. TESOL Program is a 30-unit program designed for students who wish to prepare themselves for a professional career in teaching English to speakers of other languages, in either a pre-college or post-secondary school setting, in the United States or abroad. The program offers a strong foundation in the theoretical and pedagogical aspects of the field including the study of the structure of English, language acquisition, and methods of teaching English to second language learners. The program also provides practical experience for students, such as classroom observation and student teaching in local programs, for those students without prior teaching experience.

Concentration: ['Affordable Housing and Community Development Finance', 'Applications of Technology in Planning', 'Community Design and Development', 'Environmental Planning', 'Real Estate Development', 'Transportation and Land Use Planning']
Description: The Master in Urban Planning (MUP) program trains skilled professionals who graduate with a strong education in general planning practice and theory as well as specialized training in planning subfields. [7] The program allows students to develop professional skills in an area of specialization such as Affordable Housing and Community Development Finance, Applications of Technology in Planning, Community Design and Development, Environmental Planning, Real Estate Development, or Transportation and Land Use Planning. [7] Graduates leave the program prepared with practical skills and theoretical knowledge that they can employ in jobs working to improve the quality of life and economic opportunity for all residents of urban regions as well as improving the quality of the natural environment. [7] A special mission of the program is to provide planning education opportunities for a diverse student population, including working students who prefer to attend the program on a part-time basis. [7]
Accredidation: The MUP is an accredited professional degree program nationally recognized by the Planning Accreditation Board. [7] SJSU's Masters of Urban Planning program is accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board and has consistently received high praise in their reviews. [2] Accreditation is valid through December 31, 2025. [3]

Description: The mission of the Doctor of Audiology Program in the Department of Audiology is to provide students with an academic and clinical educational program that emphasizes a solid theoretical framework and facilitates learning outstanding clinical skills for providing high-quality services to individuals with hearing and balance disorders in our community. [2, 10] Graduates of our program will be ethical; culturally sensitive; committed to evidence-based practices; prepared to assume leadership roles; and experienced in, and appreciative of, an interprofessional team approach to patient care. [2, 10] The Doctor of Audiology program, offered by the Department of Audiology, is a 4-year course of study that includes academic courses, clinical rotations, and a doctoral research project. [13] Audiology is an allied health profession that is concerned with 1) the science of the hearing and balance mechanisms; and 2) the clinical identification, diagnosis, and treatment of individuals with hearing and balance disorders. [13] The Doctor of Audiology program will prepare individuals to diagnose and treat hearing loss and other disorders involving the ear, advise patients on means to use and preserve their remaining hearing, and select and fit hearing aids and other devices. [13] Coursework includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology, hearing measurement, auditory pathology, middle and inner ear analysis, vestibular analysis and rehabilitation, rehabilitation therapies and assistive technologies, and pediatric and other special applications. [13]
Accredidation: The Doctor of Audiology (AuD) program at San José State University is accredited for the period of February 6, 2024 to February 28, 2034 by the Accreditation Commission for Audiology Education (ACAE), Office of the American Academy of Audiology, 11480 Commerce Park Drive, Suite 220, Reston, VA 20191 (703) 226-1056). [2] The doctoral program in audiology (AuD) at San José State University is a Candidate for Accreditation by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association. [2, 10] This is a “pre-accreditation” status with the CAA awarded to developing or emerging programs for a maximum period of five years. [2, 10] The program has also received approval from the CSU Chancellor's Office and from the WASC Senior College and University Commission. [5]

ProgramName: Doctor of Education in Educational Leadership
Description: The Ed.D. Program in Educational Leadership at San José State University is dedicated to developing outstanding a education a leader a who are well prepared to meet the demands and challenges of schools, today and in the future. The program builds on the following two basic principles: (1) schools are learner-centered organizations; and (2) educational leaders serve in human-care systems. The expected role of educational leaders involves creating a learning community that promotes collaboration and shared decision making. The Ed.D. Program is designed so that it may be completed in nine semesters over three years. This time frame allows for the completion of all coursework, pre proposal/literature review, dissertation proposal, and completion of the dissertation. The program begins with an intensive on-campus five-week summer session that meets three days per week. Fall and spring semester classes are scheduled as hybrid classes and meet on evenings, weekends, and online during the semester. The second summer requires a global component that includes a two-week educational and cultural experience outside of the United States. It is anticipated that students will concurrently be working full time as they pursue their doctoral studies. Additional information is available in the Educational Leadership (EdD) Program Office or website: www.sjsu.edu/edd.

The Master of Arts in Education, concentration in Curriculum and Instruction is designed for teachers and other professionals who are interested in curriculum and instruction and who wish to become curriculum leaders in the schools, and/in other educational settings. This program is appropriate for elementary, secondary, and post-secondary teachers and administrators, and for those in other professions involving training and education. The program provides a curricular and instructional core of studies for all students and then encourages students to select an area of specialization where they can focus their interests and develop expertise.

The MA in Education, Concentration in Educational Leadership is a 30-unit program designed for aspiring school administrators and leaders of other educational organizations. The program learning goals are aligned with the California Administrator Performance Expectations (CAPEs) and the national Professional Standards for Educational Leaders (PSEL), and it is accredited by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CTC). The program is designed for working professionals; we offer a two-year and a three-year program of study and our classes are held in the evenings. Our courses are taught by current and former site, district, and county-level administrators with a wealth of practical and theoretical knowledge. Upon completion of the program, students earn a MA degree in Education and a Preliminary Administrative Services Credential.
Accredidation: The program is accredited by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CTC).

Description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) is a practice degree program designed to prepare nurses at a doctoral level to lead health care change, serve as nursing faculty, and advance healthcare throughout central and northern California communities. [2] The DNP program prepares nurse leaders and advanced practice nurses for evidence-based practice in patient care, leadership, and educational roles. [2] Graduates are also prepared to serve as clinical faculty in postsecondary nursing education programs. [2] The curriculum is based on the American Association of Colleges of Nursing's The Essentials of Doctoral Education for Advanced Nursing Practice (2006) and meets all requirements for national accreditation. [2] Designed for working professionals, coursework is offered primarily in an online format with intensive sessions held on-site at the San José State University campus at the beginning of each semester. [2]
Accredidation: The curriculum is based on the American Association of Colleges of Nursing's The Essentials of Doctoral Education for Advanced Nursing Practice (2006) and meets all requirements for national accreditation. [2]

Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Advertising program is contingent upon meeting the general university admission requirements for undergraduate students. Freshman applicants must meet the California State University (CSU) eligibility requirements. [4] San José State University has not indicated any specific additional requirements such as a resume, statement of purpose, or writing sample for admission to this undergraduate program.
Department: School of Journalism and Mass Communications
Description: In the world of competitive business, companies are always looking to gain an edge for their products or services. Advertising gets them that edge. Successful modern advertising takes creativity and innovation. The School of Journalism and Mass Communications can give you the skills to make a difference in this dynamic field.
Accredidation: SJSU is accredited by the WASC Senior College and University Commission. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: Admission to San José State is competitive in all majors and is referred to as 'impaction.' This means that meeting the minimum California State University (CSU) requirements does not guarantee admission to SJSU. For the Fall 2026 admission cycle, SJSU will not consider SAT/ACT scores in the admission review. Freshman applicants who meet the CSU minimum academic requirements will be ranked in each major for admission. Preference is given to local applicants from Santa Clara County high schools. Additional consideration in the impaction process may be given to applicants who qualify for the Cal State Apply application fee waiver, are first-generation college students, or are U.S. veterans. [29] The general CSU application requires self-reporting of high school courses and may ask for information about educational programs, work, and extracurricular activities. [86]
Department: Charles W. Davidson College of Engineering
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering program at SJSU is a multi-disciplinary program that provides students with a firm foundation in the aerospace engineering fundamentals, including aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, stability and control, and space systems engineering. The program has a strong design-focus, with hands-on labs and a year-long senior design project. The program mission is to provide students with the knowledge and skills needed for a successful career in the aerospace industry or for post-graduate studies.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies
Requirements: Requirements for admission to San José State University are in accordance with Title 5, Chapter 1, Subchapter 3, of the California Code of Regulations. All CSU applications must be submitted online on the Cal State Apply website. Freshman applicants must earn a high school diploma (or equivalent), complete the required high school courses with grades of "C-" or better, and meet or exceed the CSU Minimum Eligibility Index. [21]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Animation & Illustration
Description: The award-winning Animation & Illustration BFA program, offered by the Department of Design, is committed to to providing a world-class education at an affordable price, preparing students for careers in feature film animation, games, television and any other media that uses animation and storytelling as a core communication tool. [7, 11, 12] Industry professionals and peer educators rank SJSU Animation & Illustration among the best in the nation. [7, 11, 12] The core curriculum combines both traditional and innovative educational strategies. [7, 11] Rigorous drawing classes and intensive study of color theory, design, perspective, and conventional and digital painting are required, as well as the study of the principles of both traditional and 3-D animation, physics of motion, modeling, storyboarding, character design, and visual development. [7, 11] Upper-division classes further define these disciplines offering students an opportunity to specialize in their area of choice. [5, 7, 11] All students must pass a milestone portfolio review to remain in the BFA program. [5, 7, 11] Students who were admitted as Animation & Illustration BFA and do not pass portfolio review will be changed to Design Studies, BA majors with a specialization in Animation & Illustration (ANI). [5, 7, 11] This specialization provides instruction in ANI foundation skills, supplemented by studies in design, film, photography, and theater arts. [5, 7, 11] Students receive basic preparation for entry-level jobs in the entertainment industry; optionally, they can later apply to a graduate program in Animation, Illustration or similar fields of study. [5, 7, 11] The Animation & Illustration BFA is a highly impacted major. This means that the number of applications from fully eligible students far exceeds the number of spaces available in the program. [5, 7, 11] Students interested in an impacted major must apply for admission during the initial filing period for admission in the fall. [5, 7, 11] Applications for admission to impacted majors are not accepted after the initial filing period. [5, 7, 11]

Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology program is based on general university admission requirements for first-year or transfer students. The California State University (CSU) system, including San Jose State University, bases freshman eligibility on the completion of a 15-unit pattern of college preparatory courses (referred to as “a-g” courses) and the applicant's grade point average. [64] There are no additional program-specific requirements such as a resume or statement of purpose mentioned for undergraduate admission to this specific program on the San Jose State University website.
Department: College of Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology provides a broad, cross-cultural, and holistic education that is of practical value for living in a multicultural world and of professional value for careers in a wide array of fields. Anthropology majors study human cultural and biological diversity through time and space. They develop critical thinking, writing, and analytical skills and acquire a unique perspective on the human condition that is highly valued in the 21st-century workplace. The BA in Anthropology provides students a firm grounding in the major subfields of the discipline: cultural anthropology, biological anthropology, and archaeology. It also prepares students for graduate study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology (SJSU Online)
Requirements: Applicants must meet all university admission requirements for the SJSU Online program. These include having completed at least 60 transferable semester or 90 quarter units, with a maximum of 70 semester units transferable from community colleges. Applicants must also complete the four CSU-approved general education requirements (Oral Communication, Written Composition, Critical Thinking, and Math/Quantitative Reasoning) with a grade of C- or higher, and have an overall GPA of 2.0 or better. [3, 9]
Department: College of Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology at SJSU is dedicated to understanding the human experience in all its complexity, past and present. The program is organized by the discipline’s four primary subfields: cultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. We also offer a range of courses that apply anthropological knowledge to contemporary problems. The degree program is designed to provide students with a broad and comparative perspective on human biology, society, and culture. The program provides a strong liberal arts education for students interested in a variety of careers and prepares students for graduate study in anthropology and other related fields.

This program also prepares a student for graduate study in applied mathematics, numerical analysis, or operations research. [2]

Examination of these diverse areas encourages students to become responsible citizens through an understanding of the aesthetic, cultural, and ethical choices inherent in human development. Students in this program acquire the communication skills, research techniques, and methods of critical inquiry that have become a vital part of modern life. Course offerings include a wide range of themes and topics in Modern, Contemporary, Classical, Renaissance, Islamic, and Nineteenth Century art, architecture, and design.

[3] The DMA program area teaches technical, aesthetic, and critical thinking skills to empower students as problem solvers and innovators in the field of digital technology. ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art, Photography Concentration

[11] We recognize the possibilities of the interdisciplinary nature of photographic practice and encourage interested students to explore installation, video and electronic media. [11] In addition to our emphasis on fine art photography our program includes a strong commercial photography component, offering introductory through advanced courses in studio lighting and professional practices. [11] The blend of fine art and commercial photography makes our program unique. Our technical facilities are extensive and include traditional black and white darkroom, commercial lighting studio stations, alternative practices studio, and large format digital printers. [11]
Accredidation: As a requirement of our accrediting body, the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD), all students who wish to earn a BFA in Spatial Art, Pictorial Art, Photography, or Digital Media Art must pass a portfolio review to graduate with the BFA Degree. [7]

A minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required for this coursework. Additionally, it is recommended that applicants take three to six extra units from the Pictorial Art concentration area. The final step is to pass the BFA - Art admissions review, where art faculty assess images of the applicant's creative work. [2]

It provides a mix of discipline and autonomy. Preparation begins with a strong understanding of the fundamentals of drawing. From that foundation, the aprogram provides comprehensive challenges in all pictorial disciplines and emphasizes both the historical traditions of painting and contemporary approaches. Faculty and students engage in critical and personal dialogue to encourage the development of a strong independent vision. [7]

The Studio Practice concentration serves as the foundational transfer degree program for students seeking to enter any of the professional BFA concentrations.

It is particularly appropriate for students interested in careers in social services and industry, as well as for students planning to pursue graduate studies in any of the three participating disciplines. Behavioral Science majors receive a B.A. in Social Science.

The core provides a solid background in the major areas of the discipline. Required courses in chemistry, physics, and mathematics provide the foundational knowledge necessary for a full appreciation of modern biological science. The concentrations in the diverse areas of modern biology allow students the flexibility to specialize their education to meet their individual interests and career goals. The degree provides excellent preparation for graduate study in a wide range of biological and biomedical fields and for professional careers in medicine and other health sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Sciences, Microbiology Concentration

Description: The B.S. in Biological Sciences, Microbiology Concentration is a comprehensive program that prepares students for careers in microbiology and for graduate and professional schools. Microbiologists study the morphology, physiology, genetics, and ecology of microorganisms and their applications to the fields of agriculture, industry, and medicine. The curriculum is designed to provide a broad education in the sciences and includes specialized coursework in microbiology and related disciplines. The concentration also provides hands-on training in modern microbiological, molecular, and biochemical techniques through participation in laboratory and independent research projects. After completing the core courses, students in the Microbiology concentration select from a number of upper-division electives in microbiology, immunology, virology, microbial physiology, microbial genetics, and general and medical microbiology. In addition, students are encouraged to take courses in related fields such as biochemistry, public health, and molecular biology. Students are strongly encouraged to carry out an independent research project in a faculty member’s laboratory. Students who complete an independent research project can earn credit towards graduation and can present their work at local and national scientific meetings. Graduates of the program are well prepared for graduate study in microbiology, immunology, molecular biology, and biochemistry as well as for professional programs in medicine, dentistry, optometry, pharmacy, veterinary medicine, and public health. Graduates may also choose to enter the workforce directly in the academic, government, or private sectors. Students planning a career in Clinical Laboratory Science are advised to meet with an advisor early in their program to plan their coursework.

Description: Búsiness analytics es un enfoque cuantitativo de los negocios, impulsado por el uso inteligente de datos y modelos matemáticos. Los profesionales aprovechan los métodos de la estadística y la investigación de operaciones para formular ideas y tomar decisiones que mejoren el rendimiento empresarial. El análisis empresarial es crucial para una amplia gama de industrias. Los bancos necesitan realizar análisis de riesgo de crédito y analizar las transacciones de transmisión en tiempo real para identificar rápidamente un posible fraude. Las empresas de servicios públicos necesitan analizar los datos de uso de energía para comprender mejor los patrones de demanda. Los minoristas necesitan realizar optimizaciones de rebajas, gestionar la liquidez de toda la empresa y comprender el sentimiento social en torno a sus productos y mercados para desarrollar campañas y promociones más eficaces. Business Analytics, ofrecido por el Departamento de Marketing y Business Analytics, ayuda a dichas organizaciones a descubrir conocimientos a partir de grandes datos, crear modelos que relacionen las acciones con las consecuencias y realizar análisis de optimización y simulación que conduzcan a decisiones de calidad y mejores resultados en menos tiempo. Las oportunidades laborales para los graduados con habilidades analíticas de datos nunca han sido tan numerosas. La concentración de análisis de negocios está diseñada para satisfacer esta necesidad al equipar a nuestros estudiantes universitarios con las habilidades necesarias para procesar enormes conjuntos de datos en información significativa para facilitar aún más la toma de decisiones comerciales inteligentes.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies
Department: College of Social Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Communication Studies provides students with a broad-based, liberal arts education that focuses on the symbolic and transactional nature of communication. Students are provided with a sophisticated understanding of the process of communication as it is enacted in interpersonal, group, organizational, public, and intercultural contexts. Emphasis is placed on the critical analysis of communication, and on the application of communication theories and principles to a variety of situations. Students learn how communication functions to create, maintain, and transform identities, relationships, and communities. The curriculum of the Department of Communication Studies has a three-part focus. First, it fosters an understanding and an appreciation of communication as a process. It emphasizes how communication functions to create, maintain, and transform identity, relationships, and community. Students are given the conceptual tools needed to analyze the communication process in a variety of contexts-interpersonal, organizational, intercultural, and public. Second, the program stresses a critical perspective. Students are encouraged to develop a critical sensitivity to the complexity of communication, and an appreciation for the ethical responsibilities and the potential of effective communication. Third, it is pragmatic. Students develop and improve skills in a number of areas including public speaking, argumentation and advocacy, small group communication, and interviewing.

Housed within the Department of Film and Theatre, which is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST), the program is enhanced by its interdisciplinary relationship to theatre and film and is strengthened by its connection to the vibrant arts community of Silicon Valley. Description: The BA-Linguistics program, offered by the Department of Linguistics and Language Development, undertakes the scientific study of the nature, structure and function of language. [2] Linguists study the origins of language, the meaning and history of words, variation in language, what language tells us about the workings of the human mind, and the practical aspects of language, including intercultural communication, language learning and teaching, and language as a conveyor of information in profound human arenas, such as medicine and law. [2] Linguistics is also a central discipline that is involved in communicating with machines using natural language (i.e., artificial intelligence and machine recognition and synthesis of speech). [2] The program offers state-of-the-art equipment for the acoustic and perceptual study of speech. [2] Students in the major acquire critical thinking and problem-solving skills and receive excellent preparation for advanced studies in linguistics as well as anthropology, communication, education, law, and speech and hearing. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Engineering
Description: The MatE program, offered by the Department of Chemical and Materials Engineering, stresses the roles of design, development, and process engineering, and also prepares the exceptional student for research and graduate study. [2] Materials Engineers design, characterize, and manufacture the “stuff” of our everyday world. [2, 4] Semiconductors, metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites are examples of the materials used to make everything around you - from your computer to the chair you are sitting in, from artificial body parts to the skin of the space shuttle. [2, 4] Materials scientists and engineers work in nanotechnology, biotechnology, aerospace, alternative energy, microelectronics and virtually every industry sector. [2, 4] Major areas of study are the relationships between materials' structure, properties, processing, and performance. [2, 4] The Department has excellent laboratory facilities for courses and student research. [2]
Accredidation: The Materials Engineering Bachelor of Science degree program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Program Criteria and the Materials (1), Metallurgical (2), Ceramics (3) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria. [2, 3, 5]

Description: The Bachelor of Science in Mathematics is the appropriate degree for students who wish to pursue graduate studies in mathematics and for students who are interested in a career in a mathematics-related field. Students in the program develop a strong background in the core areas of mathematics and are encouraged to broaden their mathematical interests by choosing from a list of approved upper-division electives. Students can further broaden their interests with a minor in another field.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Description: The Department of Mechanical Engineering at San José State University is the major provider of engineering talent to Silicon Valley's high-tech and cross-disciplinary industries. Our curriculum is designed to prepare our graduates for the future needs of society. The department is supported by its world class faculties, state-of-the-art laboratories–sponsored by industry–and an integrated network of professionals and alumni who provide opportunities for our students to prepare and succeed in their career. [3]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET). [3]

Description: The Bachelor of Science in Meteorology at San José State University is the only one of its kind in the California State University (CSU) system. It is a rigorous, quantitative program of study that prepares students for a wide variety of careers in the atmospheric and other environmental sciences. All students receive a strong foundation in dynamics, physical meteorology, and synoptic meteorology, consistent with the recommendations of the American Meteorological Society. The program offers two concentrations: Climate Science and Operations & Forecasting. The Bachelor of Science degree in Meteorology meets the requirements for employment as a meteorologist with the federal government as specified by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and for membership in the American Meteorological Society. The Department of Meteorology and Climate Science also offers an open account on its Linux computer network, access to its real-time weather data stream, and use of its weather analysis and display software to all majors.

The Bachelor of Arts in Music is a liberal arts degree that provides a general education in music within the context of a broad-based university education. It is designed for students who have strong musical abilities and interests but who do not necessarily wish to pursue a career as a professional performer or school music educator. The program provides the student with a foundation in music theory, music history, and performance, along with the flexibility to pursue other academic interests by taking a significant number of elective units. It is an appropriate choice for those students who wish to combine music with another field in a double major, or for those who plan to pursue a graduate degree in a field such as music history, ethnomusicology, or music theory.
Accredidation: The School of Music and Dance is a fully accredited member of the National Association of Schools of Music.

Description: The Bachelor of Music in Composition provides pre-professional training for students who, upon graduation, plan to enter a master’s degree program in composition or a related field, such as music theory, or work as a professional composer or arranger. It provides a thorough foundation in harmony, counterpoint, orchestration, analysis, and electronic music, as well as extensive work in the craft of composition. Each student composer works closely with our composition faculty, all of whom are active, professional composers. Student composers have many opportunities to have their works performed on student recitals, as well as on the yearly concerts given by the New Music Ensemble. All composition majors must present a half recital of their music in their junior year and a full recital in their senior year.
Accredidation: The School of Music and Dance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Jazz Studies
Description: The Bachelor of Music, Jazz Studies Concentration is an intensive program of study for the creative and versatile musician. The program is designed to develop the special talent of the jazz artist and to develop the flexible skills required of the successful, well-rounded professional musician. The comprehensive curriculum includes private instruction with our distinguished faculty, the study of jazz improvisation in small combo settings, and extensive courses in jazz theory, arranging, composition, and jazz history.
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Music (NASM)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Education

Concentration: ['Keyboard (piano, organ, harpsichord)', 'Voice', 'Woodwind, Brass, and Percussion', 'Strings', 'Jazz Studies']
Description: The Bachelor of Music (BM) with a concentration in Performance is a professional degree for students who show evidence of outstanding potential as performers. The curriculum is designed to develop skilled performers who are also comprehensively trained musicians. Students in this degree program will receive weekly private lessons with our nationally and internationally acclaimed faculty, participate in a variety of large and small ensembles, and perform in recitals. Upon graduation, students in this program are prepared to enter graduate school or pursue careers as professional performers and studio teachers.
Accredidation: All programs in the School of Music and Dance are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Description: The Nursing program, a department of the College of Health and Human Sciences, offers a baccalaureate degree in nursing. The program is a perfect starting point for men and women who want to make a difference in the lives of individuals, families, and communities. The mission of The Valley Foundation School of Nursing is to prepare a diverse student population to become leaders in nursing. We are committed to an inclusive and equitable learning environment, scholarship, and practice to promote health and health equity with our local and global communities.
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing at San José State University is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education, 655 K Street NW, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20001, 202-887-6791.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Science, Applied Nutrition and Food Sciences Concentration
Concentration: Applied Nutrition and Food Sciences Concentration
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Science with a concentration in Applied Nutrition and Food Sciences, offered by the Department of Nutrition, Food Science and Packaging, provides students with the education and background needed to gain employment in settings as diverse as community organizations, educational institutions, hospitals, health and fitness, nutrition and research laboratories, corporations and government agencies. [2, 6, 7] The course plan emphasizes providing a scientific foundation in introductory chemistry, bacteriology and human physiology. [2, 6] Support courses in psychology, statistics and economics also provide a strong background. [2, 6] Numerous courses in nutrition education, health in multicultural populations, community nutrition, food science, epidemiology, food safety and sanitation, cultural aspects of food, as well as nutrition, provide the industry-focused education needed for the graduates to succeed in their careers. [2] Students complete a field experience course planned for a higher level of work responsibilities with enrollment as a senior for 90 hours. [2, 6] A carefully prepared multi-year program of study will ensure an appropriate sequencing of required courses and students should seek early and frequent advice from departmental advisors. [2, 6] The BS degree in Nutritional Science with a Concentration in Applied Nutrition and Food Sciences is a regimented degree plan for students who wish to develop a focused set of skills to be successful in the community environment and the food industry. [2, 6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Science, Dietetics Concentration
Description: The Department of Nutrition, Food Science and Packaging offers a Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Science with a concentration in Dietetics. This Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) gives students a strong foundation in the competencies, knowledge, and skills required for dietetics professionals. [2] The curriculum is designed to foster critical thinking and problem-solving abilities in areas such as clinical and community nutrition, as well as food service management. [2] It also includes support courses from the social, physical, and life sciences. [2] Students can choose electives from outside the major or pursue minors in fields like business, chemistry, gerontology, or health science. [2] The program prepares students for advanced degrees (M.S.) and post-baccalaureate education, such as Dietetic Internships, and is suitable for those aspiring to become practicing nutritionists or dietitians. [2]
Accredidation: The Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) at SJSU is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics. [2] The program was reaccredited on August 7, 2020, with full accreditation for 8 years, valid until December 31, 2028. [2, 8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Science, Food Management Concentration

Description: The Bachelor of Science in Packaging program, offered by the Department of Nutrition, Food Science and Packaging, is one of a handful of programs in the USA providing technical expertise in this multidisciplinary field. [2] Every product manufactured from health care and beauty products to washing machines and drugs require packages to protect and sell the product. [2] The BS degree in Packaging is a regimented degree plan for students who wish to develop a focused set of skills in pre-selected areas of packaging so they can apply these skills in a technical setting. [2] The degree plan emphasizes industry focused scientific and methodological training, as well as breadth in pre-selected areas of engineering, graphic design, project management, advertising, and material science. [2] Students also take support courses in chemistry, math, physics, and statistics to prepare for the major. [2] A carefully prepared multi-year program of study will ensure an appropriate sequencing of required courses and students should seek early and frequent advice from departmental advisors. [2] The academic program at SJSU begins with material courses to understand the properties of glass, plastics and paper then expands to the properties and manufacturing and use of packages made from these materials. [2] The next group of courses describe the use of packages in particular industries such as food, pharmaceuticals, medical products and healthcare and beauty. [2] The courses include the corporate use of packages and project management in driving packaging projects in a firm to the understanding of federal regulations for heavily regulated industries like drugs and medical products. [2]

Philosophy is an adventure of the mind. Philosophy majors read and discuss ideas generated by some of the greatest thinkers in history, putting these ideas in conversation with each other and with contemporary concerns. The Department of Philosophy also offers Philosophy students a look at theoretical and practical problems from a philosophical perspective. Because the study of philosophy develops a student's ability to analyze ideas and arguments, to think critically, and to write well, a major in philosophy provides skills that are valued by many kinds of employers and serve as appropriate pre-professional preparation for various fields, including law, medicine, psychology and theology. Additionally, the major provides preparation for students interested in obtaining a background for graduate work in philosophy. [4, 5]

The Bachelor of Arts in Physics is intended for students who wish to obtain a solid foundation in physics but who may not intend to pursue graduate work in physics. It can be a stand-alone major, but is also well-suited for students who plan to combine it with a second major in a wide variety of other fields. For example, the BA in Physics could be a good choice for students interested in: an industrial, non-research position; a technical position in sales, marketing, or management; science writing; patent law; teaching at the high school level; or some combination of these areas. It might also be a good choice for a student who is simply interested in physics as a liberal arts major.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Political Science provides students with an understanding of politics and a set of skills for a wide variety of professions. The study of politics is concerned with the origins and nature of human conflict, the challenge of creating institutions through which conflict can be peacefully resolved, and the ever-present potential for violence. Political science is a broad discipline, covering American political institutions, the politics of the more than 180 other countries in the world, the nature of international relations, and the history of political thought from the ancient Greeks to the present. The study of political science also involves mastering a variety of research skills, such as learning how to conduct surveys, analyze election returns, and pour through historical archives. A degree in Political Science develops excellent analytical and communication skills, which are essential for a successful career in a wide variety of fields, including law, government, business, journalism, and teaching.

The Psychology major provides a broad background in the field of psychology. In addition to a core of courses that provides a foundation of knowledge in psychology, students take a number of elective courses in areas of their own interest. Many Psychology graduates go on to graduate study in psychology and other fields and to careers in social services, industrial, and other settings. The undergraduate major in Psychology prepares students for such postgraduate training and careers. A student who completes the major in Psychology should have a good grasp of the methods of science, the way in which they are applied to the study of human behavior, and a sound background of knowledge about behavior. All students receive advisement from faculty members in the department.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health
Bachelor of Science in Public Health, Community Health Education Concentration
Description: Students pursuing a BS in Public Health, offered by the Department of Public Health and Recreation, will join a group of students dedicated to documenting, monitoring, assessing, and improving the health of all communities, especially those who are marginalized. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health, Population Data Science Concentration
Description: Students pursuing a BS in Public Health with a concentration in Population Data Science, offered by the Department of Public Health , will expand on the foundational knowledge and skills provided through the core courses to explore and apply the practice of collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting data to understand and improve population health outcomes. [3]

The Bachelor's degree in Recreation is a nationally accredited program comprised of a core set of classes and courses split generally between concentration courses and major electives. [26, 31] While the general recreation degree is the most flexible in terms of choosing related electives, students may instead elect to complete a more specialized course of study in one of our two approved concentrations within the B.S. Recreation Degree: Recreation Management and Recreation Therapy. [26, 27, 31] Graduates completing one of these concentrations are eligible to apply for national and state certification. [26, 27, 31] Recreation therapy is a systematic process of treatment services that utilize recreation and other activity-based interventions to address the assessed needs of individuals with illnesses and/or disabling conditions, as a means to improve psychological and physical health, recovery, and well-being. [27]
Accredidation: The Recreation degree program has a core accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Park, Recreation, and Tourism Related Professions (COAPRT). [26, 27] The degree has maintained continuous accreditation since its first awarding of this status occurred in April 1987. [26, 27]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Recreation, Recreation Management Concentration
Description: The recreation degree program, founded in 1947 by the Department of Public Health and Recreation, has a core accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Park, Recreation, and Tourism Related Professions (COAPRT). [3] The degree has maintained continuous accreditation since its first awarding of this status occurred in April 1987, demonstrating the rigor and recognition of our programs. [3] The Bachelor’s degree in Recreation is a nationally accredited program comprised of a core set of classes and courses split generally between concentration courses and major electives. [7] Graduates completing one of these concentrations are eligible to apply for national and state certification. While the general recreation degree is the most flexible in terms of choosing related electives, students may instead elect to complete a more specialized course of study in one of our two approved concentrations within the B.S. Recreation Degree: Recreation Management and Recreation Therapy. [7] We also offer an M.S. in Recreation, which is designed to meet increasing needs and demands for recreation professionals and administrators in our growing fields of practices in public, non-profit, and commercial sectors, not only locally and regionally, but also nationally and globally.
Accredidation: The recreation degree program, founded in 1947 by the Department of Public Health and Recreation, has a core accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Park, Recreation, and Tourism Related Professions (COAPRT). [3] The degree has maintained continuous accreditation since its first awarding of this status occurred in April 1987, demonstrating the rigor and recognition of our programs. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Recreation, Therapeutic Recreation Concentration
Description: Recreation therapy is a systematic process of treatment services that utilize recreation and other activity-based interventions to address the assessed needs of individuals with illnesses and/or disabling conditions, as a means to improve psychological and physical health, recovery, and well-being. [4, 8] Graduates of recreation therapy work in a wide range of health services settings (i.e. veterans administration, mental health, addictions, physical medicine, rehabilitation, prison/corrections, pediatrics, municipal park and recreation, hospice, skilled nursing, adventure/therapeutic camps, and private practice). [4, 8]
Accredidation: The recreation degree program has a core accredited by the Council on Accreditation of Park, Recreation, and Tourism Related Professions (COAPRT). [4, 8] The degree has maintained continuous accreditation since its first awarding of this status occurred in April 1987. [4, 8]
